purpose: Additive source-backed development questions for saved per-flyer controls/options; separate from frozen retrieval and runtime/human acceptance.

questions.query: Where does the workbench save per-flyer controls and tuning, and which values win when switching models or loading a named starting setup?
facts: Private version-1 model profiles use user://workbench/flyer-profiles.json, separately from named starting setups, with a 256 KiB and 16-model bound.
Existing instances and named starts retain their explicit physical settings; saved target-model preferences supply replacements and new placements.
First flyer-to-flyer switches to an unsaved model retain the six comparison values; crossing actor kinds uses target defaults. Keyboard bindings remain private, not map content.
Preferences are saved after matching owner acknowledgement; disk failure is visible while the successful physical graph remains applied for the session.

questions.query: How can I rebind a flyer's controls or invert Kestrel side thrusters without using number keys or accidentally firing while editing?
facts: Actor options (formerly Flyer options) has primary/alternate bindings; Escape cancels capture and Delete clears a binding.
Number-row/keypad keys remain reserved, brackets cycle flyer models and Tab cycles placed instances; standard gamepad mapping is preserved.
The side-thruster inversion option reverses the existing side jets without changing A/D rotation or the rear dispenser.
The editor pauses healthy play, cancels active leases and requires neutral release before rearming; closing or accepted application restores the preceding play state when safe.

questions.query: Do the per-flyer speed, gravity, friction and movement multipliers replace the existing rigid-body actuator safety limits?
facts: Movement/body customization multiplies the copied authored profile with neutral default 1 and a 0–64 admission range.
Speed is a soft overspeed-damping target rather than a hard velocity clamp; gravity, friction and angular drag retain resolved bounds 500, 1 and 8.
Linear and angular impulse fences remain mass times 100 and inertia times 4, with existing high-speed safety braking.
Preferences do not alter native material/contact laws or the source authored flyer definitions.

questions.query: Is the new pixel thruster exhaust real Fire, and how are per-flyer dispenser materials and fractional spawn amounts bounded?
facts: Cosmetic exhaust derives from live actuator telemetry and creates no material; the real Fire toggle separately inserts native Fire ID 6.
Existing authored dispenser ports can select registered materials 1–131 except 10, or 0 to disable; preferences cannot add a missing port.
One-times requests one cell per nozzle every six ticks; 0–8 amounts use a deterministic fractional pulse schedule with at most three nozzles per body and 24 queued intents.
Every destination/path is checked under the 64-iteration trace and 1024-read/body bounds; hard terrain, foreign masks and occupied endpoints can reduce output without overwriting material.
